issue_context.title: SQL: Conjunction with comparison of datetime field to date string incorrectly yields no results
issue_context.body:
The following query incorrectly yields no results:

```
select hire_date from test_emp where hire_date > 'now-25y' and hire_date < '2021-09-01'

   hire_date
---------------
```

Expected result is equal to the result returned by only using the first condition:

```
select hire_date from test_emp where hire_date > 'now-25y'

       hire_date
------------------------
1999-04-30T00:00:00.000Z
1997-05-19T00:00:00.000Z
1996-11-05T00:00:00.000Z
```

The second condition matches all records in the test_emp table.

Interestingly, not all conjunctions with this kind of comparison fail in this way:

```
select hire_date from test_emp where hire_date > 'now-25y' and hire_date < 'now/y'

       hire_date
------------------------
1999-04-30T00:00:00.000Z
1997-05-19T00:00:00.000Z
1996-11-05T00:00:00.000Z
```

review_comments: Based on the conversion, the value should always be a datetime otherwise one ends with an invalid comparison.

Thank you @costin, I created a new issue about this https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/87500

About the check on `value`, actually the value is never involved in this comparison (not in this method at least), so there is no risk to have false positives due to it (on the other hand, false negatives are tolerated, eg. for date maths).
